findings.title: float: right on button is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container
findings.body: .small-action was changed to `@include flexbox()`, but its direct child `button { float: right; }` (line ~306-309) still relies on floating. Floats have no effect on flex items, so the button (e.g. the 'delete' action on small-actions) will no longer be pushed to the right edge; it will sit immediately after the description text. It should be replaced with `margin-left: auto` inside the flex container. The `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc .avatar` similarly no longer does anything.

findings.title: -ms-align-items is not a real property
findings.body: The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. There is no such CSS property; the Microsoft pre-flexbox property is `-ms-flex-align` (already emitted on the previous line). This dead declaration just bloats the compiled stylesheet on every use of the mixin and suggests the vendor prefix list was copied without verification. It should be removed.

findings.title: .valign-helper vertical centering hack breaks inside the new flex container
findings.body: `.d-header .contents` is now a flex container (`@include flexbox()` + `align-items(center)`), but the legacy `.valign-helper { display: inline-block; height: 100%; vertical-align: middle; }` (lines 21-25) remains. In a flex container `vertical-align` is ignored and `height: 100%` resolves against the container's content-box height, so the helper no longer vertically centers its siblings the way it did in the old inline/float layout. Any markup still relying on valign-helper (e.g. in plugins or older header markup) will render misaligned. The rule should be removed or converted to flex-based centering.

findings.title: order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper only works when its parent is the flex header
findings.body: `.extra-info-wrapper` now uses `@include order(2)` with no accompanying display change, so `order` only has an effect when the element happens to be a direct child of a flex container (the header `.contents`). Everywhere else `.extra-info-wrapper` appears (it is also used outside the header, e.g. above the topic list in category pages) the declaration is inert. If reordering is only intended in the header, it should be scoped as `.d-header & { @include order(2); }` to make the intent explicit; otherwise the non-header usages silently keep their DOM order and any layout change there is unintended.
